description: Make AI food and drink videos from a single bottle or can photo: a slow pour, ice, and fizz in a 9:16 clip for TikTok and Reels. Upload your photo to start.
h1: Make AI Food and Drink Videos From a Bottle Photo
lead: AI food and drink videos turn a photo of your bottle or can into a close-up pour with ice, bubbles, and fresh fruit. Get a 6, 10, 15, or 30 second vertical clip made for scrolling feeds.
intro: A quick, close-up pour is the whole idea: your drink flowing from bottle to glass. The sample shows sparkling orange juice splashing over ice next to a sliced orange, with whole fruit on a cutting board behind it.

A short pour puts the drink's color, fizz, and texture in motion. Use it for juices, sodas, cold brew, kombucha, sauces, or syrups. A 6-second clip can show one pour, while 10 seconds leaves room for a slower pour and a final look at the full glass.
tip: Upload a photo with the bottle upright and the liquid color visible, then mention the glassware, the ice, and what sits on the counter.

steps.d: A straight-on photo lets the video carry the shape and liquid color into the pour.
Describe the glass, garnish, and surface, like "tall glass, crushed ice, lime wedge, marble counter." Pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.
Add flavor names, prices, and sound in Canva or CapCut, since letters in AI video can come out garbled.

ideas.d: Swap the orange slice for berries or a cinnamon stick when a new seasonal flavor comes out.
Try honey over pancakes, hot sauce over tacos, or syrup swirling into iced coffee.
Make a 1:1 version to sit next to your still photos in a Shopify product gallery.

faq.q: What kinds of drinks work with this?
faq.a: Anything you pour: juice, soda, sparkling water, iced tea, cold brew, and mixers. Clear glass bottles and bright liquids tend to look the most striking.

faq.q: Will my label come out clearly?
faq.a: Small print may not be perfect. Keep the label facing the camera in your photo, and if the brand name needs to be crisp, add it as text in your editing app.

faq.q: How do I keep the drink color believable?
faq.a: Photograph the can or bottle in even light and name the real color in the prompt. Review the pour against the product; AI can drift on liquid color and label details.

overview.h2: Make the liquid do the explaining
overview.d: A strong pour scene has three anchors: the package, the receiving food or glass, and one visible texture change. Ask for the liquid to flow, fizz, foam, or glaze while keeping the label and product color in view.

overview.h2: Use the short version for the first sensation
overview.d: Six seconds can capture an opening splash or a quick drizzle; ten, fifteen, or thirty gives the viewer more time to see ice settle, foam rise, or a full glass reach its final level. Keep one pour per clip so the action stays legible.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a package for a pour scene

items.d: A straight bottle, can, pouch, or jar photo gives the generated scene a stable shape to carry into the counter setup.
For translucent drinks or sauces, use a view where the liquid color is visible instead of hidden behind a dark label.
Name a tumbler, coupe, bowl, plate, or spoon so the pour has a clear destination and scale.
Say crushed ice, foam, fizz, syrup ribbon, or glaze; one texture cue gives the shot a specific job.

results.h2: What the finished pour can show

items.d: The package stays part of the composition while the liquid moves into a glass, bowl, or over food.
Choose 9:16 for TikTok or Reels, 1:1 for a product gallery, 16:9 for a wider placement, or 4:3 and 3:4 for another crop.
Six, ten, fifteen, and thirty seconds cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits; the charge is visible before you submit.

scene_recipes.h2: Pour scenes for food and drink products

items.d: A chilled bottle pours into a tall glass with orange peel, cubes, and a bright counter catching the bubbles.
Dark coffee folds into milk over a clear glass beside a small jar of beans and a spoon.
A squeeze bottle lays a glossy line of chili sauce across a finished noodle bowl from above.
Golden honey trails from a jar onto warm toast, ending with the jar and crumbs in the same frame.

after_download.h2: Add the details your offer needs

items.d: Add the exact name, size, price, or launch date in a clear text layer.
Pair the pour with licensed music or a satisfying sound effect in your editing tool.
Review the glass, garnish, and package before publishing so the scene matches the product you sell.
